Before you begin

This game is built around three real presidential broadcasts, 1962 to 1969, and the American rooms that heard them. Tonight's evening includes the real address announcing Soviet missiles in Cuba. Later evenings include war, the draft, and the documented deaths of named civil-rights workers, presented as records, never as imagery.

Nothing jumps at you. Nothing is timed. You can stop at any break and carry your place out. The doorway out is always one keypress: the Home link, top left.

This game questions rhetoric, routines, and concealment. It never questions service, or the people and families who served.

Draft copy - founder voice pass owed before ship (cyl-full-bible.md, section 15).

Transcript - the address, as heard tonight

John F. Kennedy, Radio and Television Report to the American People on the Soviet Arms Buildup in Cuba, October 22, 1962. A work of the United States federal government: public domain. Tonight's broadcast is an excerpt; the full address is public record and its complete transcript ships with the founder-supplied sound clip.
